page0.text:
"Forget it. You're Sakura's enemy. I can't trust you to watch my back."
"I see. I thought I would be of help. A pity."
The priest stops following me.
...I can't afford to stop here.
I need to catch up to Sakura as soon as possible.

page1.text:
It's dawn by the time the taxi arrives at the forest.
If you think it's sketchy for a high schooler to be taking a taxi at 3:00 AM, imagine him asking you to drop him off in the woods outside of town.
After hailing no less than twelve cabs, I finally find a driver willing to take me. The sun is starting to rise by the time I arrive at the forest entrance.

page2.text:
...This is my second time in these woods.
I rely on my memory to find the Einzbern castle.
...I couldn't reach it the last time I was here.
On the way to the castle, I ran into Illya fleeing the Shadow.

page3.text:
...
...I check my left arm.
It's completely different since the last time I was here.
I was helpless as the Shadow nearly slaughtered me.
That hasn't changed.
I have no way to beat Sakura—no, the Shadow, and it has Saber on its side, too.

page4.text:
...If I run into them, I'm done.
The only way to take Illya back is to ambush them.
I need to retrieve Illya without Sakura noticing me.
In that case...

page5.text:
In that case, what should I do?
How should I deal with Sakura now that she's changed?
How can I turn her back into the Sakura I used to know?

page6.text:
"..."
I don't have an answer.
All I can do is follow after them as quickly as I can.

page7.text:
I see a familiar place.
It's been a little over two hours since I entered the woods.
The sun is already well over the horizon, but the forest is still shrouded in fog.

page8.text:
...Last time, this was as far as I went.
If the visions Illya showed me are true, then I should be at the castle soon.
Almost there.
Just a little more until I enter enemy territory...

page9.text:
I get through the forest.
I'm in a circular clearing in the vast sea of trees.
The castle I saw through Illya's "eyes" towers over the forest, just as I remember.

page10.text:
There's no sign of anyone around.
It's strange that there's no guards on the castle walls, to say nothing of the castle, but I can't turn back now just because this might be a trap.

page11.text:
Going through the front gate... is out of the question.
If I'm going to sneak in, then I should use a window on the second floor or higher.
"...I'll head around back. If push comes to shove, I'll use the back door."
There isn't anyone guarding the back of the building.
I climb up a sturdy-looking tree, and break in from the second floor.

page12.text:
"Whoa!"
I break a window as I jump into the building.
The castle is deathly silent, even after my violent entry.

page13.text: "...Are they not even paying attention? Maybe they don't see me as a threat. Or maybe..."

page14.text:
Zouken and Sakura might have already left.
...That would explain the lack of any security.
It's already been a full day since Sakura took Illya away.
I don't know why they came out here, but they had plenty of time to finish whatever they came to do.

page15.text:
"...No, there's someone here. Plus..."
The castle is filled with a bizarre aura.
An overwhelming torrent of magical energy coils around my skin like fog.
...There's no doubt.
This magical energy belongs to the version of Sakura I saw at my house, with the strange markings taking over her body.

page16.text:
"It's getting thicker the lower I go..."
Sakura's on the first floor.
...I could look for the stairs down, but I should find Illya first.
I'm screwed if Sakura is with her, but she might be imprisoned somewhere in the castle. I need to get her out of here before our showdown with Sakura.

page17.text:
None of the castle doors or gates are locked.
I go from the second floor to the third, then the fourth.
I search every nook and cranny for any sign of Illya.

page18.text:
Now I'm deep within the fourth floor.
I step into a room that looks like a warehouse. It's different than the rest.

page19.text:
"Illya, are you there...?"
I call out in a hushed voice.
There are things scattered everywhere, making it hard to see. Maybe this is a storage room.

page20.text:
"..."
If Illya isn't here, then I can only presume she's on the first floor with Sakura—

page21.text:
"Who's there!?"
I whirl around at the sound of footsteps.
Someone steps through the door.
It's a familiar-looking woman in a white dress.

page22.text:
"Oh, you're..."
Illya's other caretaker, whom she called Sella.

page23.text:
"Welcome home, Master Emiya. My mistress says that she will not be meeting you."
"Uh... Wait, you mean Illya...!?"
"...Please address her as Lady Illyasviel. You have no right to be so familiar with her."

page24.text:
...
I'm taken aback by her icy tone.
"That is all my mistress told me to relay to you. If you value your life, then hurry. You will die if you stay here, Master Emiya."
Sella gives me a courteous farewell bow.

page25.text:
"Hey, wait! Hold on, Sella!"
"..."
Sella stops and looks at me. She seems surprised that I used her name.

page26.text:
"Was there anything else? I must decline to provide you with the locations of my mistress or your friend. I was asked only to deliver a message."
Sella cuts me off coolly.
...Seeing the way she acts, I falter.

page27.text:
...
I gasp, but not because of her attitude.
...They're so similar.
I'm not sure why I think so, but Sella resembles Illya.
Her face, demeanor, build, and age are all different, but I can't help but see them as sisters.

page28.text: "...If that is all, then farewell. I ask that you do not waste Lady Illyasviel's goodwill."

page29.text:
"Ah... It's not like that, Sella. I'm here to help Illya, but I don't want to cause trouble for you.
It's your job to take care of her, right? Then you know that we need to rescue her from this castle."

page30.text:
"You forget your place.
But you are correct. As you say, my mistress must escape this place as soon as possible."
Yeah! So tell me where—

page31.text:
"I cannot do that. Even if I told you, it would be futile."
Sella quietly leaves.

page32.text:
"Hey, wait! I'm...!"
It happens in an instant.
A pitch-black dagger flies at me from where Sella was just standing.

page33.text:
"Mmph, ah..."
I stagger.
Blinded by the pain, I retreat to the window.
In front of me,
floats a white skull mask.

page34.text:
"Hah... nrgh...!"
I feel for the window with my hand.
...But what will I do if I find it?
This is the fourth floor, and there's a knife deep in my chest.
I'm losing so much blood that I probably won't even last another minute.

page35.text:
"You actually came alone, you despicable fool."
"...Haah..."
"I am not like my Lord Mage. I will put you out of your misery quickly."

page36.text:
"...Guh...!"
I wrench myself towards the windowsill.
I don't care that I'm on the fourth floor.
I try to run from the reaper closing in on me...
...but as soon as I reach for the window, a blade slides into my neck.

page37.text:
The skull goes blurry.
"Sleep now. It may not save you from your sorry state, but it is still far better than being eaten by that monster."
My vision grows dim.

page38.text:
...On the cusp of death, I feel regret.
Even if I was in a race against time, it was still too reckless to come alone.
